intro: Picture waking up and walking just a few minutes to the shore of Kwan Phayao, the freshwater lake in the middle of town with mountains as a backdrop, then coming back in the evening to sip coffee by the hotel pool as the sun slips behind the hills — Green Hill Hotel Phayao is a budget-friendly 3-star hotel planted on Phaholyothin Road in central Phayao, within walking distance of Kwan Phayao · what people keep mentioning is the in-town location within walking distance of the lake, clean and spacious rooms, an outdoor pool with views of the lake and mountains, and free parking, all at a price that feels genuinely reachable · open since around 2016, the building is still fairly new, with rates from about THB 900–1,400/night · near Wat Sri Khom Kham, Wat Analayo Thipayaram, and Phayao Walking Street · review scores sit around 8.0–8.1 from real guests, with most of the praise going to cleanliness and the pool.

body.html: Who Green Hill Hotel Phayao suits — to put it as briefly as possible, Green Hill Phayao is an in-town hotel for anyone who wants to stay near Kwan Phayao on a budget while still getting a pool and free parking thrown in · it isn't a luxury lakeside resort selling premium peace and quiet, and it isn't a design-heavy boutique in the old town · it's a fairly new 3-star hotel sitting on Phaholyothin Road in central Phayao, a few minutes' walk from the lakeshore · open since around 2016 and still running today, bookable through Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com, and the usual major travel platforms · real reviews line up on who fits here: road-trippers driving around the north who stop in Phayao for a night or two, families wanting a pool for the kids to splash in, people on official business or work in Phayao town, and couples or groups of friends who like to wake up and cycle or stroll along the lake in the morning · another group that says they're happy is anyone after a clean in-town hotel with easy parking and a fair price, rather than full-service amenities like a big Bangkok hotel · honestly, if you set your expectations to match the price and size of this place, most people come back with a positive review.

Location and getting around — this is the main selling point of Green Hill Phayao · the hotel sits at 356/1 Phaholyothin Road, Wiang Subdistrict, Mueang Phayao, the main road that runs through the center of town · what a lot of people love is that it's within walking distance of Kwan Phayao, the largest freshwater lake in the upper north and the symbol of the province · wake up and walk a few minutes and you're at the lakeside esplanade, where you can stroll, cycle, or sit with a coffee taking in the lake and the mountains · within walking distance of the hotel there are plenty of restaurants, coffee shops, and convenience stores to choose from, and it's close to important temples like Wat Sri Khom Kham (Wat Phra Chao Ton Luang), just a few minutes' drive away · if you want to go on to Wat Analayo Thipayaram on Doi Busarakham, or to Phayao Walking Street on Friday and Saturday evenings, getting there is easy because you're in the middle of town · for longer journeys, Phayao has no commercial airport of its own, so most people drive in themselves or fly into Chiang Rai Airport (CEI) and continue by car for about 1.5 hours, or fly into Chiang Mai and drive about 3 hours · one thing to note: the hotel sits right on Phaholyothin Road with traffic passing all the time, so rooms facing the road catch some traffic noise, which many reviews mention.

"It's only a few minutes' walk from the hotel to the Kwan Phayao lakeside. We'd wake up early to walk and catch the cool breeze, then come back and swim in the hotel pool. Great value for the price · parking was easy too, no driving around to find a spot."

Room types and decor — Green Hill Phayao has rooms across several tiers, sorted mainly by view and bed type · starting with the Standard City View rooms, available with either a large bed (Double) or twin beds (Twin), good for couples or friends travelling together · stepping up to the Lake View / Pool View rooms, which look out onto the pool and Kwan Phayao as a backdrop — these are the ones many people recommend if your budget allows, because the view is the charm of this place · the decor is a simple, contemporary style in easy tones, not luxurious but clean and new in line with the building's age · every room has air conditioning, a fridge, an LED TV, free drinking water, blackout curtains, and a private bathroom with a water heater · plenty of reviews agree on the same point: the rooms are very clean, the beds are comfortable, and they're more spacious than you'd expect at this price, which is the highest-scoring aspect of the hotel from real guests · some international reviews note that small items are missing from certain rooms, such as a safe or a hairdryer, so it's worth bringing your essentials or asking at the counter first · if you're sensitive to noise, it's best to request a room not facing Phaholyothin Road at the time of booking, because the inner-facing or pool-side rooms are clearly quieter.

Facilities and the pool — the most talked-about highlight of Green Hill Phayao is the outdoor pool by the lake · plenty of reviews agree the pool is fairly large and prettier than expected for a hotel in this price range, looking out over Kwan Phayao and the mountains as a backdrop, especially in the evening when the setting sun catches the water · it's a spot where families bring the kids to swim, and people who like taking photos usually go home with good shots · besides the pool, downstairs there's a poolside cafe/coffee shop for drinks and breakfast · other facilities include free parking, which many praise as convenient and roomy enough, a lift, a 24-hour reception counter, daily housekeeping, and free Wi-Fi · to be honest, there's no fitness center, spa, or luxury-resort-level amenities here, because it's a mid-sized in-town hotel focused on simplicity and value · but for a one- or two-night stay while touring Phayao, what's on offer is enough and matches what you pay.

Food and the cafe — food is where you need to set the right expectations · the hotel has a poolside cafe/coffee shop serving breakfast and drinks · from real reviews, breakfast here is the simple kind, served by the pool, and some reviews — international tourists in particular — note that the breakfast options are limited and the portions fairly small, so this isn't the place to expect a big buffet · the upside of the central location is that just stepping out around the hotel you'll find local eateries, noodle shops, coffee shops, and food stalls along Kwan Phayao to choose from, so many people end up heading out for breakfast and other meals, which is part of the charm of staying in town · if you come on a Friday or Saturday evening, Phayao Walking Street by the lake is another spot for tasty local food at friendly prices · overall, food isn't the main reason people choose to stay here, but the location, where it's easy to walk out and find something to eat, makes up for it a fair bit.

Service — service is where reviews are fairly mixed, and it's worth knowing before you check in so you set the right expectations · on the praise side, plenty of reviews say the staff are polite, friendly, and helpful, handling parking and check-in smoothly · but to be straight about it, some international reviews note that most of the staff are young and speak limited English, so it can be hard to communicate if you need more complex help, and at times there's no manager or senior staff on duty · for Thai travellers, language usually isn't an issue, but foreign visitors may need a translation app to help · overall, the service is at a usable level for a budget 3-star hotel, and suits a stay where you don't need to lean on extra services much.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulled together from Trip.com, Booking.com, and Tripadvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: rooms cleaner and more spacious than the price suggests, comfortable beds, a large and lovely pool with lake views, an in-town location within walking distance of Kwan Phayao, convenient free parking, and good overall value · on the watch-out side: the thing that comes up is noise from Phaholyothin Road — the hotel sits right on the main road, so rooms facing the street catch some traffic noise, followed by breakfast with limited options and small portions, some reviews mentioning a smell from the drains at certain spots at certain times, staff with limited English, and small items like a safe or hairdryer missing from some rooms · most of these gripes are manageable by choosing a room not on the street, bringing your own essentials, and setting expectations to match the price, rather than being big problems that put people off returning · the highest-scoring aspects — cleanliness and the pool — are what pull the overall score up to around 8.0–8.1.

"Clean room, comfortable bed, a lovely pool with lake views · the only gripe was that our room faced the road and we heard a bit of traffic at night, so next time we'll ask for a pool-side room instead · breakfast was ordinary but it's easy to walk out and find food."

Price and value — the starting rate for a Standard room is around THB 900/night at normal prices (it can dip below that during promotions), rising to about THB 1,200–1,400+ for a Lake View / Pool View room, or during long weekends and festivals when lots of people are visiting Phayao · compared with other hotels and stays in Phayao town, most of which are small properties or guesthouses, Green Hill feels like good value among budget in-town hotels, especially once you factor in a pool with lake views, free parking, and a location within walking distance of Kwan Phayao, which aren't easy to find at this price point · if you're planning to stop in Phayao for a night or two on a northern road trip, the money you spend on the location and the pool comes back as good value · but if you're after a luxury lakeside resort with full-service amenities, this isn't that tier, and you should consider a higher-end stay instead.

Good to know before booking — a few things make the stay smoother · one, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, specify at booking that you want a room not facing Phaholyothin Road; pool-side or inner rooms are quieter · two, if the lake view matters to you, choose a Lake View / Pool View room from the start because it's the charm of this place · three, don't expect a big breakfast buffet — plan to head out for local food around Kwan Phayao instead, which is more filling and more fun · four, bring small personal items yourself, like a hairdryer, in case the room you book doesn't have one · five, Phayao has no commercial airport, so most people drive in themselves or continue by car from Chiang Rai for about 1.5 hours; plan your route and parking ahead (the good news is there's free parking here) · six, during long weekends and festivals rooms fill up fast, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms.

The bottom line — from all the real reviews, Green Hill Hotel Phayao is the best fit for anyone who wants to stay in Phayao town near the lake on a budget, with a pool and free parking · clean, spacious rooms, a pool with views of the lake and mountains, and a location within walking distance of Kwan Phayao make it good value among the town's budget stays · if you're after a luxury lakeside resort, full-service with fluent English-speaking staff, or a varied breakfast buffet, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a higher-end stay · but for a northern road trip where you want to stop in Phayao for a night or two in a good location at a fair price, with a pool overlooking the lake to unwind by — Green Hill Phayao answers that need well for its price, which is why review scores still hold around 8.0–8.1 from real guests.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Green Hill Hotel Phayao

faq.q: Where is Green Hill Hotel Phayao · can you walk to Kwan Phayao?
faq.a: The hotel is at 356/1 Phaholyothin Road, Wiang Subdistrict, Mueang Phayao, in central Phayao · it's within walking distance of Kwan Phayao, the lake in the middle of town, a few minutes' walk away · near Wat Sri Khom Kham, Wat Analayo Thipayaram, and Phayao Walking Street · Phayao has no commercial airport, so most people drive in themselves or continue by car from Chiang Rai for about 1.5 hours.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Green Hill Hotel Phayao · what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 900/night for a Standard City View room at normal prices (it can be cheaper during promotions) · there are Lake View / Pool View rooms from about THB 1,200, and higher-tier/family rooms around THB 1,400 · prices rise during long weekends and festivals, so it's worth comparing several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Green Hill Hotel Phayao have a pool and parking?
faq.a: There's an outdoor pool that many reviews call larger and prettier than the price, with views of Kwan Phayao and the mountains, plus a poolside cafe · and there's free parking, which is convenient and ideal for road-trippers · there's also a lift, a 24-hour counter, and free Wi-Fi, but no fitness center or spa.

faq.q: Who is Green Hill Hotel Phayao good for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for road-trippers touring the north who want to stop in Phayao, families wanting a pool for the kids, and people on business in Phayao town who want a clean, budget-friendly stay with parking, within walking distance of the lake · if you're after a luxury lakeside resort with full-service amenities, a higher-end stay may suit you better.

faq.q: What are noise and breakfast like at Green Hill Hotel Phayao?
faq.a: The hotel is right on Phaholyothin Road, so rooms facing the street catch some traffic noise; it's best to request a pool-side or inner room not facing the road if you're a light sleeper · breakfast is the simple kind served by the pool with limited options, and many people head out for local food around Kwan Phayao instead.

faq.q: What's Green Hill Hotel Phayao's review score · is it open?
faq.a: It is currently open, bookable through Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com · review scores sit around 8.0–8.1 from real guests (Booking.com around 8.0, Trip.com around 8.1), praised mainly for cleanliness, spacious rooms, and the pool with lake views, while the main watch-outs are noise from the road and a simple breakfast.
